_comment: Battlefield banner bearers. Drives the engine's native BannerBearerLogic, which is already present in every field battle, sally-out and siege. Edits require a full game restart (config is cached for the process lifetime).
_comment_MinimumFormationTroopCount: Formations smaller than this never raise a banner. Engine floor is 2; valid range 2-100.
_comment_MaxBearersPerFormation: Hard ceiling per formation. Valid range 1-6 — the engine's bearer arrangement tables only hold 6 positions.
_comment_BannerPerSoldiers: One banner per N soldiers, per formation class. 0 disables banners for that class. Note: extra bearers add visual density and redundancy (the banner effect survives a bearer dying) — the formation bonus itself does NOT stack.
_comment_ExcludedRaces: Races that never carry a standard. Race ids come from LOTRLOME_Armory/ModuleData/skins.xml. Named races are heroes anyway (the engine already excludes heroes) and are listed for belt-and-braces.
_comment_CultureBanners: Culture StringId -> banner ItemObject id. Vanilla banner items are neutral-culture with using_tableau=true, so the cloth always renders the party's own heraldry — the item picks a pole/cloth silhouette and a BannerComponent effect tier, it does NOT lock the faction. Map a culture to "" to give it no banner. Custom LOTR banner meshes can be swapped in later by changing ids here, with no code change.
_comment_CultureBanners_ids: KEYS ARE StringIds, NOT display names. TAOM re-skins the six vanilla cultures via spcultures.xslt, which overrides <name> but NEVER the id — so Rohirrim = 'vlandia', Dunlendings = 'empire', Haradrim = 'aserai', Easterlings/Rhun = 'khuzait', Barding/Dale = 'sturgia', Variag/Khand = 'battania'. Using the LOTR name as a key silently gives that faction the default banner instead.
_comment_DefaultBannerItemId: Fallback for any culture not listed above. Empty by design (fail closed): 38 cultures are registered but only the 28 above are TAOM's — the rest are vanilla leftovers still referenced by live data (looters, sea_raiders, forest_bandits, desert_bandits, mountain_bandits, steppe_bandits, nord, vakken, darshi) plus neutral_culture. Naming a banner here hands one to ALL of them — e.g. looters raising the Gondorian Standard of Duty. A forgotten culture with no banner is a cosmetic absence; with the wrong banner it is an immersion break.
